self.title: Message yourself
self.body: Talk to SynaBun in your own "Message yourself" chat. No second number, nothing to buy: scan one QR code and write.

notes.0: SynaBun reads that one chat only; every other chat is ignored.
notes.1: Only messages typed on your phone count: what you type into "Message yourself" from WhatsApp Web or Desktop is ignored.
notes.2: Replies start with "SynaBun:". WhatsApp may not notify you of messages in your own chat.

dedicated.title: A second number
dedicated.body: Link a spare WhatsApp account (a second SIM, or WhatsApp Business on another number) and chat with it like a contact. Your own account is never linked.

notes.1: Needs a second number that can receive WhatsApp. You prove it is you with a one-time claim code.

read-only.title: Read-only
read-only.body: SynaBun answers, researches and plans. It never changes files, runs commands or starts agents from WhatsApp; a plan can only be approved on this computer.

ask.title: Ask on my phone
ask.body: Before anything that would change your files, run a command or start an agent, SynaBun asks on WhatsApp and acts only on your yes. Any other message approves nothing: the conversation just carries on.

autonomous.title: Autonomous
autonomous.body: SynaBun acts without asking, like the Assistant on this computer. Turning it on takes a second click here and an ALLOW code sent from your phone within 5 minutes. It turns back to Ask after 8 hours. Autonomous can read any file your computer account can, including SynaBun's WhatsApp login. Use it only with a locked phone, ideally on a second number.

limits.2: Messages older than 10 minutes when SynaBun comes back online are skipped (it tells you how many).
limits.3: Answers are split into messages of 3,500 characters; the rest stays in SynaBun.
limits.4: Computer use from WhatsApp is off until you turn it on above. Then: never at Read-only or while paused, after one yes per task at Ask on my phone, and without asking while Autonomous is active. Agents started from WhatsApp never get it.

help.how: SynaBun links to WhatsApp the same way WhatsApp Web does: as a linked device of an account. Messages you send in the chosen chat reach the SynaBun Assistant on this computer, and its answers come back as WhatsApp messages. Your computer has to be on and SynaBun running.

2.2: One QR scan + a claim code

help.unofficial: This uses an unofficial connection (Baileys), not the WhatsApp Business API. WhatsApp's Help Center warns that using unofficial apps "may result in a temporary or permanent account ban". SynaBun keeps traffic low and only ever writes to you, but the risk is not zero; the second-number mode keeps it off your own account.
help.linkedDevice: A linked device can see every chat of the account. SynaBun receives them from WhatsApp and ignores them: only your chat with SynaBun is read, and nothing else is stored.
help.lostPhone: Lost your phone, or something looks wrong? Press Pause now here, or on any device open WhatsApp → Settings → Linked devices, tap SynaBun and Log out.
help.downloads: The connector is downloaded from the npm registry the first time you set up WhatsApp (a few seconds), pinned to exact versions: baileys (MIT) and its dependencies, among them libsignal (GPL-3.0). It is installed in its own folder and runs as a separate process; it is not part of SynaBun's own code. The pin is baileys 7.0.0-rc14: older versions are deprecated for CVE-2026-48063.

troubleshooting.0: WhatsApp allows 4 linked devices. If linking fails, remove one under Linked devices on your phone.
troubleshooting.1: If your phone is offline for 14 days, WhatsApp logs out every linked device. Link again when that happens.
troubleshooting.2: Replies in "Message yourself" usually do not notify you; use the second-number mode if you need notifications.
troubleshooting.3: In "Message yourself", only messages typed on the phone reach SynaBun. Messages typed into that chat from WhatsApp Web or Desktop are ignored.
troubleshooting.4: With "Only messages that start with sb", a note without sb never reaches SynaBun and is not logged; commands, the ALLOW code and replies to SynaBun's messages always get through.
troubleshooting.5: The QR code expires after about a minute. Press "Show a new code" and scan faster, or link with your phone number instead.
troubleshooting.6: Stuck on "Reconnecting"? Check this computer's internet connection, then press Reconnect now.

help.browserTools: Not the same as the WhatsApp browser tools. The whatsapp MCP profile lets agents read WhatsApp Web in SynaBun's browser; this tab is you chatting with SynaBun from your phone. They do not share a session.
help.uninstall: Uninstalling SynaBun does not unlink WhatsApp. Use Unlink or Remove here first, or log SynaBun out under WhatsApp → Settings → Linked devices.

onboarding-explore.title: Start with your project
onboarding-explore.body: SynaBun can read one of your projects now and save what it learns as memories. You can also do this later in {settings} → {projects}.

onboarding-token-warning.title: Exploration uses tokens
onboarding-token-warning.body: A coding CLI reads your files and writes the memories with the model you pick. Check your plan's limits before you start.

onboarding-cli-picker.title: Choose your coding CLI
onboarding-cli-picker.body: Pick one that is installed and signed in on this machine. It is used for the exploration only.

onboarding-model-picker.title: Choose a model
onboarding-model-picker.body: The exploration runs on the model you pick here. The CLI default works too.

onboarding-project-picker.title: Choose a project
onboarding-project-picker.body: The exploration runs in the folder you pick. If it is missing, add it in {settings} → {projects}.

onboarding-memory-explain.title: Ready to explore
onboarding-memory-explain.body: The CLI opens in a terminal window and saves memories as it reads. Your agents recall them in later sessions and update them as the code changes.

welcome.title: A quick tour of your workspace
welcome.body: See how memory, your coding tools and the SynaBun Assistant fit together. Skip whenever you like: the ? button brings you back.

explain-memory-explorer.title: Find what your agents remember
explain-memory-explorer.body: {explorer} lists every saved memory. Search it, or filter by category and tag.

explain-graph.title: See your memory as a map
explain-graph.body: Each memory is a point on the map, and categories form islands. The {menu} menu frames it, shows a memory's neighbours and rebuilds the layout.
explain-graph.body2d: Each memory is a node, linked to the memories related to it. The {menu} menu picks which links show and how many memories load, and resets the layout.

explain-focus.title: Make room to think
explain-focus.body: Focus mode swaps the {view} for a whiteboard. Draw and write here: your agents can read the board and add to it.
explain-focus.graph: {focus} swaps the {view} for a whiteboard. Draw and write there: your agents can read the board and add to it.

explain-workspaces.title: Keep your layout
explain-workspaces.body: A workspace saves your open cards, your view and your filters. Load it to get that scene back.

explain-terminals.title: Work with your coding CLIs
explain-terminals.body: {apps} opens Claude Code, Codex, Gemini and OpenCode in terminal windows. Dock them at the bottom or float them over the board.

explain-browser.title: Bring the browser along
explain-browser.body: {apps} → {browser} opens the browser SynaBun controls. Your agents use it to read pages and act on them.

explain-side-panel.title: Chat beside your work
explain-side-panel.body: These buttons open Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode as side panels. Pick a project and a model there and start chatting.

explain-automations.title: Give repeatable work a home
explain-automations.body: {studio} keeps the tasks your agents repeat as templates. Launch one with the CLI and model you choose.

explain-schedules.title: Run work at the right time
explain-schedules.body: {schedules} runs your automations on a timer or a cron schedule. Each run opens its own agent session.

assistant-start.title: Meet the SynaBun Assistant
assistant-start.body: Tell it what you need in plain words; it asks when something is unclear. Try “What can you help me do in this project?”
assistant-start.closed: This button opens the Assistant. Tell it what you need in plain words; it asks when something is unclear.

assistant-tools.title: Small jobs, done right here
assistant-tools.body: It browses, runs shell commands, makes small edits and manages memory, loops and schedules itself. The {computer} switch lets it use the apps on your Mac.
assistant-tools.closed: It browses, runs shell commands, makes small edits and manages memory, loops and schedules itself. In its toolbar, the {computer} switch lets it use the apps on your Mac.

assistant-route.title: Big jobs go to workers
assistant-route.body: Coding, design, image and video jobs go to Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode workers. A route card picks the model for each one; this switch sets when it asks you.
assistant-route.closed: Coding, design, image and video jobs go to Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode workers. A route card picks the model for each one, and you set when it asks you.

assistant-track.title: Follow the work
assistant-track.body: Every run a worker does shows up in the chat with its result. This strip counts the tokens used, and {more} → {budget} caps the spend.
assistant-track.more: Every run a worker does shows up in the chat with its result. Token use is counted below the chat, and {more} → {budget} caps the spend.
assistant-track.closed: Every run a worker does shows up in the chat with its result. The Assistant counts the tokens used, and {more} → {budget} caps the spend.

explain-help.title: Come back whenever you like
explain-help.body: ? reopens this tour where you left off. {keybinds} lists your shortcuts, and {settings} holds everything else.

skip-hint.title: Your tour lives here
skip-hint.body: Click ? whenever you want to pick it up again. Nothing in your workspace was changed.
